headline: Mostly dry through Friday, then a cooler pattern brings frost chances Saturday morning and returning showers from Saturday into next week.
summary: Western Washington stays mostly dry through the end of the week. Wednesday afternoon turned sunny, with highs in the mid and upper 60s and a couple of 70s in the south. A weak cold front passes Thursday morning with more clouds but no rain expected. Behind it there is a 20 percent chance of isolated showers Thursday afternoon, mainly in the south interior and south Sound. Friday clears in the afternoon and is a few degrees cooler, with highs in the mid to upper 50s. Saturday morning is expected to be the coldest of the stretch, with lows widely in the 30s and a chance of frost, especially in the south interior. How much frost forms depends on how long skies stay clear Friday night. Over the weekend a low-pressure system aloft is expected to drop south into the Pacific just off the coast, bringing a chance of showers from Saturday through the middle of next week. Snow levels, the elevation where rain turns to snow, may briefly fall to about 3,000 to 4,000 feet on Saturday, so some mountain snow showers are possible. Forecasters do not expect rainfall amounts to cause significant impacts. After Saturday, temperatures and snow levels are favored to warm slightly. The Pacific coast may see breezy winds again Sunday, but winds are otherwise expected to stay light. Forecasters are fairly confident in the dry stretch through Friday and in Saturday being coldest, but less sure about the weekend and next week because computer models disagree on whether the low stays off the coast or moves away and lets high pressure build in. No watches, warnings or advisories are in effect for land areas. Small Craft Advisories for the Pacific coastal waters run from Thursday into Friday, with seas of 10 to 15 feet Thursday night and northwest coastal gusts of 25 to 35 mph.
changes: The early-morning discussions expected a weak, uncertain weekend system with falling rain chances. By afternoon, forecasters added a cold Saturday morning with frost chances and possible mountain snow showers, and described a low off the coast bringing showers from Saturday through the middle of next week.
